description:
should_gc counts on-heap young bytes only. A process that makes large binaries (over SHARED_BIN_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 64, runtime/src/heap/mod.rs:83) puts a 32-byte ProcBin stub on the heap and the bytes off-heap (Heap::alloc_bitstring, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:855). The dead stubs, and so the off-heap bytes, are freed only at a collection, which those 32-byte stubs alone rarely trigger.
Measured on c5a03e198 and develop: String.duplicate("abcdefgh", 16000) makes 15,992 shared binaries totalling 1,024,063,712 bytes with zero fz.runtime.gc events and a 1.17 GB peak RSS (GC heap a few MB). Peak RSS 34 MB / 100 MB / 1117 MB at 8/32/128 KB of input. Repro: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/repro/binwalk.fz, dup.fz, bwstats.fz.
BEAM counts referenced off-heap binary bytes as virtual heap and collects when it overflows. Experiment first, with predictions: count live stub bytes into the trigger; measure peak RSS on the repro and the distiller and instructions on the suite. Interacts with fz-9x7.7 (minimum young size) and fz-sc8.208 (binary views).

The measurement above used the quadratic String.duplicate that develop replaced in PR #588 (a939d32e8), so most of those bytes were its intermediate results. The trigger gap still holds by construction, but the numbers must be re-measured on develop with a repro that makes dead large binaries directly, and again after fz-sc8.208 lands (about 560 -> 140 stubs per distiller line).

comments.text: Refuted after five pre-registered rounds (scratch 9x7-8/notes.md, results{,2,4,5}.txt, page https://claude.ai/artifact/QydSk1Cp2zZs8PiAqix8sp). Rounds 2-3: young binary bytes in the heap trigger (256 B floor) cut deadbinlive RSS 202->73 MB with every guard in range. Round 4: that variant regresses survive vs today (168->230 MB); old-binary majors (A) cost the distiller 4.0x RSS / 1.22x instructions; quantum cut (B) costs deadbin 2.14x instructions. Round 5 (OTP-shaped separate binary budgets, 256 KiB minimum, judged vs today, 147 runs/variant): F, O, F+C, O+C all fail rules 2 and 3 on dist-p28000 (RSS 1.74-1.77x), dist-full (RSS 3.98-4.35x, instr 1.20-1.27x), json (RSS 1.15-1.22x, instr 1.09-1.14x) and rule 2 on survive (instr 1.19-1.26x). The quantum cut at a 256 KiB minimum works: quantum 125 MB -> 0.3 MB off-heap at no instruction cost. Mechanism of the distiller regression is unverified; the only clause F, O and round-4 A share is the old-binary major.
Reopened (user approved page https://claude.ai/artifact/PC7vJ3veeQqqQca2ppEnWp): revisit as round 6 on the aged collector of fz-9x7.11; round 6 is pre-registered when fz-9x7.11 lands.

title: Off-heap binary bytes count toward the collection trigger
